title: Smooth proper homogeneous quotient under a self-normalizer hypothesis
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $G\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A group scheme over $S$ is a group object in schemes over $S$ [def-pc-scheme], with the multiplication, identity and inverse diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over this base. Let $H\hookrightarrow G$ be a finitely presented closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] which is smooth over $S$ with nonempty geometrically connected fibres [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after extension to an algebraic closure of each residue field. Assume that $G$ has geometrically connected fibres and that $H$ is self-normalizing: for every $S$-scheme $W$, an element $g\in G(W)$ satisfying $c_g(H_W)=H_W$ lies in $H(W)$. Let $Q$ be the fppf sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $W\mapsto G(W)/H(W)$, where fppf coverings [def-pc-fppf-site] are jointly surjective families of flat morphisms locally of finite presentation. Then $Q$ is represented by a smooth $S$-scheme $X$. The projection $G\to X$ is a smooth surjective right $H$-torsor: $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$ identifies $G\times_SH$ with $G\times_XG$. These quotient and torsor identifications commute with arbitrary base change. If for every geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ the sheaf $G_{\bar s}/H_{\bar s}$ is represented by a projective $\Omega$-scheme, then $X\to S$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Here projective means admitting a closed immersion into $\mathbf P^n_\Omega$ for some $n\geq0$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], and geometric point means [def-weil-geometric-point].

source.place: Conrad, Theorem 2.3.6(1),(2) and proof, printed pp.72--75; the paragraph beginning the proof notes local sections of G to G/H for smooth H. Quotient base change and the torsor identity are the functorial sheaf-quotient consequences. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this relative group-scheme assertion.

proof.text: Let $H$ act on $G$ on the left by $h\cdot g=gh^{-1}$. This is free: $gh^{-1}=g$ implies $h=1$. Smoothness makes $H/S$ flat and locally finitely presented by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Apply [lem-sfb-free-flat-group-space-quotient] with base $B=S$ and $Z=G$. Its orbit presheaf is exactly the right-coset presheaf in the statement. Thus $Q$ is an algebraic space, $q:G\to Q$ is surjective, flat and locally finitely presented, and has fppf local sections on each scheme test. Replacing the action variable by its inverse and exchanging the two factors in the relation gives the isomorphism $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$ from $G\times_SH$ onto $G\times_QG$.

source.place: Tag 06PH, lemma-quotient-free-action; left action h.g=g h^{-1}

proof.text: For a scheme $T\to Q$, write $P=G\times_QT$. A local lift $a:T_i\to G$ of its section identifies $P\times_TT_i$ with $H\times_ST_i$ by $h\mapsto ah$; the inverse sends $b$ to $a^{-1}b$, which belongs to $H$ by the relation isomorphism of step 1. These are inverse maps of sheaves on every test scheme. The fppf-locality and base-change assertions of [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality] show that $P\to T$ is smooth. Therefore $q$ is smooth in the chartwise sense. To see $Q/S$ locally of finite type, apply [lem-sfb-space-lft-smooth-fpqc-locality](iii) with smooth source cover $G\to Q$, target cover $S\to S$, and $G\to S$ locally of finite type (smooth implies locally finitely presented).

The diagonal of $Q/S$ pulls back along the fppf cover $G\times_SG\to Q\times_SQ$ to the closed subscheme $G\times_QG\subset G\times_SG$: it is the inverse image of $H\subset G$ under $(g,b)\mapsto g^{-1}b$. The cover is fppf by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus], using the flat locally finitely presented surjection of step 1 twice. Closed immersions are stable under base change and descend along such covers by [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-fppf-descent]. Hence $Q/S$ is separated. Its relative diagonal is quasi-compact, since a closed immersion is affine (the scheme-test affine description of [def-weil-closed-immersion]). As $S$ is affine, [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] shows that $Q$ is quasi-separated. Also $Q$ is quasi-compact: its point space is the continuous surjective image of the quasi-compact scheme $G$, by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. This last assertion follows directly by pulling an open cover back to $G$ and taking a finite subcover.

source.place: Tag 041F, lemma-descending-property-closed-immersion; diagonal of a quotient by a closed subgroup

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-finite-jet-normalizer-detection] and work on one of its affine opens $U$. Write $C\twoheadrightarrow D$ for the finite free coordinate-algebra quotient of $H_n\subset G_n$, of ranks $M$ and $r$. By [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective], rank-$r$ quotients of $C\simeq\mathcal O_U^{M}$ are classified by a projective Grassmannian $P=G_U(M,r)$ with distinguished point $\xi$ given by $D$. Conjugation on $G_n$ acts on $C$, hence on its quotient functor and therefore on $P$. The stabilizer of $\xi$ on a test scheme $W$ consists exactly of $g$ preserving $(H_n)_W$ as a closed subscheme. The finite-jet lemma identifies this with the normalizer of $H_W$, which is $H(W)$ by the hypothesis of the item. Consequently $g\mapsto g\xi$ is constant on right $H$-cosets and extends uniquely to a map $i:Q_U\to P$ by the sheafification universal property; the target $P$ is an fppf sheaf by [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf], since fppf coverings are fpqc coverings by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. It is a monomorphism: locally lift two sections of $Q_U$ to $g,b\in G(W)$; equality of their images says $g^{-1}b\in H(W)$, hence their cosets agree. Equality of sections descends because $Q_U$ is a sheaf. Local lifts and equality in the sheafification are justified by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local].

source.place: Theorem 2.3.6 proof, p.74: Grassmannian orbit map through the finite-jet quotient

proof.text: The Grassmannian $P$ is quasi-compact and separated over the affine $U$: it is projective and [lem-pc-projective-proper] makes it proper. Its absolute quasi-separatedness follows from [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products]. By step 3 the same quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness hold for $Q_U$ (apply that argument over $U$). The map $i$ is locally of finite type by [lem-sfb-space-lft-cancellation], since $Q_U\to U$ is locally of finite type. Thus [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-lft-mono-quasiaffine] makes $i$ quasi-affine, in particular representable by schemes. Since $P$ is a scheme, so is $Q_U$. On $U_i∩ U_j$, both scheme pullbacks represent the same restricted sheaf $Q$, giving canonical isomorphisms with identity and triple-cocycle equalities. Apply [lem-galois-glue] over the open cover $\{U_i\}$ of $S$ to obtain an $S$-scheme $X$. The local sheaf isomorphisms $h_X|_{U_i}\simeq Q|_{U_i}$ glue uniquely, since $Q$ is a sheaf, and give $h_X\simeq Q$.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.6 proof, p.74: monomorphism into the Grassmannian and the quasi-affine consequence of Zariski Main

proof.text: Now $q:G\to X$ is a flat surjective locally finitely presented map of schemes, and the composite $G\to X\to S$ is the given smooth structural map. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] to conclude that $f:X\to S$ is smooth. Step 2 already proved that $q$ is smooth; step 1 gives its surjectivity and right $H$-torsor relation. Both $X$ and $S$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by step 3. Then [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $f$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated; smoothness supplies local finite presentation, so $f$ is of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 05B5, lemma-smooth-fpqc-local-source; finite presentation = qc + qs + lfp

proof.text: For any $S'\to S$, the map $G_{S'}\to X_{S'}$ has fppf local sections on scheme tests by pulling back those of step 1, and its relation is $G_{S'}\times_{S'}H_{S'}$ by the same base change of the displayed isomorphism. Hence $G_{S'}/H_{S'}\to X_{S'}$ is an isomorphism of sheaves: a section on the right locally lifts to $g$, and two local lifts yield the same section exactly when their ratio belongs to $H$. This is precisely the local-section and local-equality characterization of sheafification in [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local]. The relation map remains $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$, since pullback retains multiplication. Thus the quotient and torsor identifications commute with arbitrary base change; no assertion that the presheaf quotient is already a sheaf is needed.

source.place: Tags 00WB, theorem-plus, and 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification; apply the local description after base change

proof.text: Assume now the projectivity hypothesis. Step 7 identifies every geometric fibre of $X/S$ with the stated projective quotient, so it is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. It is nonempty and connected: $G_{\bar s}\to X_{\bar s}$ is a continuous surjection and its source is nonempty and connected by hypothesis (nonemptiness comes from the identity). The image of a connected space is connected, since a disconnection pulls back to a disconnection. Apply [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] for continuity and surjectivity on point spaces. To prove properness over the arbitrary ring $A$, use [lem-sfb-space-proper-strict-local-test], applicable since step 6 gives finite presentation. Fix a geometric point and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $R=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$. The ring $R$ is local and henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure]. Base change preserves finite presentation and separatedness by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] and [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition], and preserves smoothness by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality].

source.place: Tag 08K1, lemma-eventually-proper, strict-local properness test; Conrad Theorem 2.3.6 proof, pp.74-75, connected proper fibres

proof.text: Write $Y=X\times_ST$. Its closed fibre $Y_0$ is proper: it becomes a projective geometric fibre after an algebraic closure of the residue field, and properness descends along that faithfully flat field extension by [lem-sfb-space-proper-fpqc-descent]. The pair $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ is henselian. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-henselian-proper-clopen-lift] to the entire closed fibre to obtain an open and closed subscheme $Z\subset Y$, proper over $T$, with $Z_0=Y_0$. The map $Z\to T$ is also flat and locally finitely presented, since $Y/T$ is smooth and restriction to an open preserves smoothness by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes], followed by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Thus its image is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] and closed by properness. It contains the closed point, so it is all of the local scheme $T$. Every geometric fibre of $Z/T$ is therefore nonempty. It is open and closed in the corresponding connected geometric fibre of $Y/T$, so it is that whole fibre. The complement $Y\setminus Z$ has no point, hence is empty, and $Y=Z$ is proper. The strict-local test from step 8 now proves $X/S$ proper. This argument also handles non-Noetherian and nonreduced $A$; for $A=0$ all schemes and assertions are empty.
